key_insight: In 2D glasses under cyclic shear, the cycles-to-failure diverge near the fatigue limit with an exponent close to -1, indicating a dimensionality-dependent fatigue law and a robust link between accumulated plasticity and eventual failure.
engineering_relevance: This suggests that fatigue life prediction in disordered solids may depend strongly on spatial dimension, while plastic-damage metrics like dissipated work and non-affine motion can help monitor degradation before failure.
method: Atomistic simulations of two-dimensional model glasses under cyclic shear deformation
Measured failure time versus strain amplitude near the fatigue limit
Computed accumulated plasticity indicators such as dissipated work and non-affine displacements
Performed isoconfigurational seeded simulations with an introduced localized soft region
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a power-law divergence of cycles-to-failure with exponent near -1, and that dissipated work and non-affine displacement scale with failure time in a manner consistent with 3D results.
watch_item: Seeding localizes where failure occurs but does not remove the broad scatter in failure times, so deterministic lifetime prediction remains limited.
paper_title: Fatigue failure in two-dimensional glasses under cyclic shear deformation
